title: अध्याय ९३

items.text:
एतत्ते कथितं भूप देवीमाहात्म्यमुत्तमम् ।
एवंप्रभावा सा देवी ययेदं धार्यते जगत् ॥ १ ॥
items.tr:
etatte kathitaṃ bhūpa devīmāhātmyamuttamam |
evaṃprabhāvā sā devī yayedaṃ dhāryate jagat || 1 ||
items.speaker: ; ऋषिरुवाच

items.text:
विद्या तथैव क्रियते भगवद्विष्णुमायया ।
तथा त्वमेष वैश्यश्च तथैवान्ये विवेकिनः ।
मोह्यन्ते मोहिताश्चैव मोहमेष्यन्ति चापरे ॥ २ ॥
items.tr:
vidyā tathaiva kriyate bhagavadviṣṇumāyayā |
tathā tvameṣa vaiśyaśca tathaivānye vivekinaḥ |
mohyante mohitāścaiva mohameṣyanti cāpare || 2 ||

items.text:
तामुपैहि महाराज शरणं परमेश्वरीम् ।
आराधिता सैव नृणां भोगस्वर्गापवर्गदा ॥ ३ ॥
items.tr:
tāmupaihi mahārāja śaraṇaṃ parameśvarīm |
ārādhitā saiva nṛṇāṃ bhogasvargāpavargadā || 3 ||

items.speaker: ; मार्कण्डेय उवाच
items.text:
इति तस्य वचः श्रुत्वा सुरथः स नराधिपः ।
प्रणिपत्य महाभागं तमृषिं शंसितव्रतम् ॥ ४ ॥
items.tr:
iti tasya vacaḥ śrutvā surathaḥ sa narādhipaḥ |
praṇipatya mahābhāgaṃ tamṛṣiṃ śaṃsitavratam || 4 ||

items.text:
निर्विण्णोऽतिममत्वेन राज्यापहरणेन च ।
जगम सद्यस्तपसे स च वैश्यो महामुने ॥ ५ ॥
items.tr:
nirviṇṇo'timamatvena rājyāpaharaṇena ca |
jagama sadyastapase sa ca vaiśyo mahāmune || 5 ||

items.text:
संदर्शनार्थमम्बाया नदीपुलिनसंस्थितः ।
स च वैश्यस्तपस्तेपे देवीसूक्तं परं जपन् ॥ ६ ॥
items.tr:
saṃdarśanārthamambāyā nadīpulinasaṃsthitaḥ |
sa ca vaiśyastapastepe devīsūktaṃ paraṃ japan || 6 ||

items.text:
तौ तस्मिन् पिलिने देव्याः कृत्वा मूर्ति महीमयीम् ।
अर्हणां चक्रतुस्तस्याः पुष्पधूपाग्नितर्पणैः ॥ ७ ॥
items.tr:
tau tasmin piline devyāḥ kṛtvā mūrti mahīmayīm |
arhaṇāṃ cakratustasyāḥ puṣpadhūpāgnitarpaṇaiḥ || 7 ||

items.text:
निराहारौ यतात्मानौ तन्मनस्कौ समाहितौ ।
ददतुस्तौ बलिं चैव निजगात्रासृगुक्षितम् ॥ ८ ॥
items.tr:
nirāhārau yatātmānau tanmanaskau samāhitau |
dadatustau baliṃ caiva nijagātrāsṛgukṣitam || 8 ||

items.text:
एवं समाराधयतोस्त्रिभिर्वर्षैर्यतात्मनोः ।
परितुष्टा जगद्धात्री प्रत्यक्षं प्राह चण्डिका ॥ ९ ॥
items.tr:
evaṃ samārādhayatostribhirvarṣairyatātmanoḥ |
parituṣṭā jagaddhātrī pratyakṣaṃ prāha caṇḍikā || 9 ||

items.text:
यत्प्रार्थ्यते त्वया भूप त्वया च कुलनन्दन ।
मत्तस्तत्प्राप्यतां सर्वं परितुष्टा ददामि तत् ॥ १० ॥
items.tr:
yatprārthyate tvayā bhūpa tvayā ca kulanandana |
mattastatprāpyatāṃ sarvaṃ parituṣṭā dadāmi tat || 10 ||
items.speaker: ; श्रीदेव्युवाच
; मार्कण्डेय उवाच
items.text:
ततो वव्रे नृपो राज्यमविभ्रंश्यन्यजन्मनि ।
अत्रैव च निजं राज्यं हतशत्रुबलं बलात् ॥ ११ ॥
items.tr:
tato vavre nṛpo rājyamavibhraṃśyanyajanmani |
atraiva ca nijaṃ rājyaṃ hataśatrubalaṃ balāt || 11 ||

items.text:
सोऽपि वैश्यस्ततो ज्ञानं वव्रे निर्विण्णमानसः ।
ममेत्यहमिति प्राज्ञः सङ्गविच्युतिकारकम् ॥ १२ ॥
items.tr:
so'pi vaiśyastato jñānaṃ vavre nirviṇṇamānasaḥ |
mametyahamiti prājñaḥ saṅgavicyutikārakam || 12 ||

items.text:
स्वल्पैरहोभिर्नृपते स्वं राज्यं प्राप्स्यते भवान् ।
हत्वा रिपूनस्खलितं तव तत्र भविष्यति ॥ १३ ॥
items.tr:
svalpairahobhirnṛpate svaṃ rājyaṃ prāpsyate bhavān |
hatvā ripūnaskhalitaṃ tava tatra bhaviṣyati || 13 ||
items.speaker: ; श्रीदेव्युवाच

items.text:
वैश्यवर्य त्वया यश्च वरोऽस्मत्तोऽभिवाञ्छतः ।
तं प्रयच्छामि संसिद्ध्यै तव ज्ञानं भविष्यति ॥ १५ ॥
items.tr:
vaiśyavarya tvayā yaśca varo'smatto'bhivāñchataḥ |
taṃ prayacchāmi saṃsiddhyai tava jñānaṃ bhaviṣyati || 15 ||

items.speaker: ; मार्कण्डेय उवाच
items.text:
इति दत्त्वा तयोर्देवी यथाभिलषितं वरम् ।
बभूवान्तर्हिता सद्यो भक्त्या ताभ्यामभिष्टुता ॥ १६ ॥
items.tr:
iti dattvā tayordevī yathābhilaṣitaṃ varam |
babhūvāntarhitā sadyo bhaktyā tābhyāmabhiṣṭutā || 16 ||

items.text:
एवं देव्या वरं लब्ध्वा सुरथः क्षत्रियर्षभः ।
सूर्याज्जन्म समासाद्य सावर्णिर्भविता मनुः ॥ १७ ॥
items.tr:
evaṃ devyā varaṃ labdhvā surathaḥ kṣatriyarṣabhaḥ |
sūryājjanma samāsādya sāvarṇirbhavitā manuḥ || 17 ||

items.h: इति श्रीमार्कण्डेयमहापुराणे सावर्णिके मन्वन्तरे देवीमाहात्म्ये वरप्रदानं नाम त्रिनवतितमोऽध्यायः

en_summary: The sage ends the story of the goddess's greatness for King Suratha: such is the power of the goddess who upholds this world; by Vishnu's Maya the king, the merchant and other wise people are deluded, have been deluded and will be deluded. He tells the king to take refuge in this highest goddess, who when worshipped gives enjoyment, heaven and final freedom. Markandeya says that, hearing this, King Suratha, tired of his strong attachment and of the loss of his kingdom, bowed to the sage and went at once to do penance, and so did the merchant. To see the Mother, they stayed on a river bank, where the merchant chanted the highest hymn to the goddess (Devi Sukta). They made a clay image of the goddess on the river bank and worshipped it with flowers, incense, fire offerings and water offerings; fasting, with controlled and fixed minds, they also gave her offerings sprinkled with blood from their own bodies. After three years of such worship, Chandika, the upholder of the world, appeared before them pleased and offered whatever they wished. The king chose a kingdom that would not be lost in another life, and in this life his own kingdom back, won by force after destroying his enemies' power. The merchant, whose mind had turned away from the world, chose the knowledge that removes the attachment of 'mine' and 'I'. The goddess told the king that in a few days he would regain his kingdom by killing his enemies and it would stay secure; and that after death he would be born again from the Sun god (this verse is incomplete in the text). To the merchant she gave the knowledge he wanted, for his final success. Having given both their wishes, and praised by them with devotion, she vanished. So, having received the goddess's boon, Suratha, the best of kshatriyas, will be born from the Sun and become the Manu Savarni.
